titleEn: Condo Renovation Permit Guide for Metro Vancouver 2026: Strata Approval, Building Permits and Municipal Rules
titleZh: 大温哥華分契物業装修許可指南2026：strata审批、建筑許可證與市政規定
contentEn:
Renovating a condo in Metro Vancouver requires navigating two parallel approval systems: your strata corporation approval under the BC Strata Property Act, and the municipality building permit. Both are mandatory and one does not replace the other. Starting work without both can result in stop-work orders, fines, and the cost of reversing unapproved changes.

Strata approval and municipal permits are separate processes. The strata council approves whether your renovation is permitted under your building bylaws and the Strata Property Act. The city or municipality approves whether the work complies with the BC Building Code, local building bylaws, and fire and safety standards.

BC Strata Property Act: What Requires Strata Approval in 2026

Under the Strata Property Act (RSBC 1998, c.43), certain renovations require a 3/4 vote of eligible voters at a general meeting. These are called significant changes and include any work that affects the common property, the building exterior, or the structural elements of the strata lot.

Reno Stars typically handles two categories of work requiring strata approval: alterations that change the exterior appearance of a unit (such as adding built-in cabinetry that alters walls, replacing flooring in a way that affects load distribution, or modifying balcony enclosures), and any work that requires penetrations into common property walls, floors or ceilings.

Renovations that typically require only strata council approval (not a 3/4 vote) include cosmetic work that does not affect common property or the building systems, such as painting walls, installing shelving, and replacing bathroom fixtures in the same positions.

Vancouver Building Permit Requirements for Condo Renovations

The City of Vancouver Building Bylaw requires a building permit for any condo renovation that involves structural changes, changes to fire separations, modifications to plumbing or electrical systems, or any work that requires an inspection under the BC Building Code.

Building permits are required for: removing or altering load-bearing walls, adding or relocating plumbing fixtures (moving a sink, toilet or shower requires a permit), any electrical work beyond simple receptacle replacement, installing new flooring that changes floor assembly composition (such as replacing vinyl with ceramic tile, which affects structural load), and modifications to fire-rated walls or assemblies.

The City of Vancouver permit application requires: architectural drawings or sketches showing existing and proposed conditions, a letter of acknowledgement from the strata corporation confirming strata approval, BC Building Code compliance documentation for any structural or fire-safety related work, and for certain projects an engineer assessment stamped by a BC registered professional.

Municipal Permit Rules Across Metro Vancouver

Each municipality in Metro Vancouver has its own building bylaw that sets permit thresholds and inspection requirements. The baseline is the BC Building Code, but municipalities add local amendments.

Vancouver requires permits for flooring material changes, plumbing fixture relocations, and any structural modification. Burnaby mirrors Vancouver requirements and additionally requires engineering review for floor assembly changes in wood-frame buildings. Richmond requires a strata acknowledgement letter before issuing permits for any work in strata properties. Surrey requires permits for any work affecting fire separations and has additional requirements for buildings with sprinklers. Coquitlam requires permits for any work affecting the building envelope, including window replacement and balcony enclosure modifications.

The Strata Approval Process: Step by Step

The strata approval process begins with reviewing your strata corporation bylaws. Every strata has a bylaws document that specifies what requires approval. Obtain a copy of Form B (the Information Certificate) which lists the current bylaws and any recent resolutions affecting renovations.

Submit a renovation application to the strata council. This should include: detailed descriptions of all proposed work, drawings or plans showing the scope of work, any required engineering documentation, and the contractor insurance certificate and business licence.

The strata council has up to 30 days to respond to renovation applications under the Strata Property Act. If the council does not respond within 30 days, the application is considered approved. However, if the work requires a 3/4 vote, the application must go to a general meeting, which adds 4-6 weeks to the timeline.

Keep records of all strata correspondence, including the original application submission date and any written approvals. These records are essential when selling your unit, as a lawyer or notary will typically request evidence of proper approvals for any renovation work.

Common Condo Renovation Permit Mistakes to Avoid

The most common mistake is assuming that strata approval alone is sufficient to begin work. Strata approval does not replace the municipal building permit. Both are required. A second common mistake is beginning work before obtaining written strata approval, which can result in the strata council ordering work to stop and requiring removal of completed improvements at the owner expense.

A third mistake is failing to verify whether the proposed work is actually permitted under the strata bylaws. A renovation may technically require strata approval even if the strata council is willing to grant it. The bylaws may prohibit certain types of work outright. Review the bylaws before designing the renovation.

Finally, failing to update the Form B information certificate after completing major renovations can cause problems when selling. The Land Title and Survey Authority of BC requires that any material changes to a strata lot be reflected in updated documentation.

Frequently Asked Questions

Do I need both strata approval and a building permit for my condo renovation in Vancouver?

Yes. The strata corporation approval under the BC Strata Property Act and the municipal building permit are separate requirements. Both are mandatory. Strata approval does not replace the building permit and building permit does not override strata bylaws. Reno Stars handles both processes as part of every condo renovation project in Vancouver.

What happens if I renovate my condo without strata approval?

The strata corporation can issue a formal order requiring you to stop work and restore the unit to its original condition at your expense. In serious cases the strata may apply to BC Supreme Court for an injunction. When you sell the unit the unapproved renovation may need to be disclosed and the buyer can negotiate a price reduction or require restoration as a condition of sale.

How long does strata approval take in BC?

The strata council has 30 days to respond to a renovation application. If the renovation requires a 3/4 vote at a general meeting, add 4-6 weeks for notice and scheduling. The entire process from application to written approval typically takes 6-10 weeks for routine renovations and up to 4 months for renovations requiring a general meeting vote.

Does the City of Vancouver require a building permit for flooring replacement in a condo?

Yes, if the new flooring material is significantly heavier than the existing flooring. Replacing vinyl sheet flooring with ceramic tile, natural stone, or concrete topping requires a building permit in Vancouver because it changes the floor assembly load. The structural engineer assessment confirms whether the existing floor system can support the new material. Lightweight flooring replacements (vinyl to vinyl, carpet to carpet) typically do not require a permit.

Can Reno Stars handle the strata approval process for my condo renovation?

Yes. Reno Stars has managed condo renovation projects throughout Metro Vancouver, including Burnaby, Richmond, Surrey, Coquitlam and Vancouver. We prepare the strata application package, coordinate with strata councils, and handle the municipal permit process as part of our standard project management service.

Planning a condo renovation in Vancouver, Burnaby, Richmond, Surrey, Coquitlam or another Metro Vancouver city? Contact Reno Stars for a free estimate -- strata approval, municipal permits and construction all managed under one contract.

在大溫哥華裝修分契物業（condo）需要同時滿足兩個審批系統的要求：根據《卑詩省分契財產法》取得的strata corporation審批，以及市政府頒發的建築許可證。兩者缺一不可，且兩者不能互相替代。在未獲得這兩項批准的情況下開工，可能導致勒令停工通知、罰款，以及自行拆除未批准工程的費用。

《卑詩省分契財產法》：2026年哪些工程需要Strata審批

根據《分契財產法》（RSBC 1998，第43章），若干裝修工程需要在大會上獲得3/4合格選票的批准。這些被稱為「重大」變更，包括任何影響共用財產、建築外觀或分契單位結構元素的工程。

聚星裝修通常處理的工程可分為兩類：需要strata審批的工程（不一定需要投票），以及需要3/4投票的工程。需要投票的工程包括：影響共用財產的工程、改變建築外觀的工程，以及影響樓宇結構的工程。

通常只需strata理事會審批（無需投票）的工程包括：不影響共用財產或建築系統的裝飾工程，如牆面油漆，安裝擱板，以及在不變動位置的情況下更換衛生間設施。

溫哥華分契物業裝修的建築許可證要求

溫哥華市建築附例要求，對於涉及結構變更、改變防火隔離、修改管道或電氣系統，或任何需要根據《卑詩省建築規範》進行檢查的工程，必須申請建築許可證。

需要建築許可證的工程包括：拆除或改動承重牆、添加或移動衛生間設施（移動洗手盆、馬桶或淋浴間需要許可證）、任何超出簡單插座更換範圍的電氣工程，以及改變地板組成的工程（例如用瓷磚更換乙烯基地板，這會影響結構負荷）。

溫哥華市許可證申請需要：顯示現有和提議條件的建築圖紙或草圖、strata corporation確認strata審批的認可函、《卑詩省建築規範》合規文件，以及某些工程需要卑詩省註冊專業工程師加蓋印章的工程評估。

大溫哥華各市許可證規則對比

大溫哥華每個城市的建築附例都規定了許可證門檻和檢查要求。本拿比的要求與溫哥華類似，但對木框架建築的地板組裝工程有額外的工程審查要求。列治文要求在任何strata工程頒發許可證之前必須提供strata認可函。素里對影響防火隔離的工程有附加要求，高貴林要求對任何影響建築圍護結構的工程（包括窗戶更換和陽台圍封）申請許可證。

Strata審批流程：逐步指南

Strata審批流程的第一步是審查strata corporation的附例。每個strata都有一份附例文件，規定哪些工程需要審批。獲取B表格（信息證書）的副本，其中列出了當前的附例以及任何影響裝修的最新決議。

向strata理事會提交裝修申請。申請應包括：所有擬議工程的詳細說明、顯示工程範圍的圖紙或計劃、任何必需的工程文件，以及承包商的保險證書和商業執照。

根據《分契財產法》，strata理事會有最多30天的時間回覆裝修申請。如果理事會未在30天內回覆，申請被視為已獲批准。但是，如果工程需要3/4投票，申請必須提交到大會，這會將時間表延長4-6週。

常見錯誤

最常見的錯誤是假設只需strata審批就可以開工。Strata審批不能替代市政建築許可證。兩者都是必需的。第二個常見錯誤是在獲得書面strata批准之前就開始工程，這可能導致strata理事會下令停工，並要求業主自費恢復原狀。

第三個常見錯誤是未能確認擬議工程是否在strata附例允許範圍內。即使strata理事會願意批准，裝修在技術上可能仍需要strata審批——附例可能明確禁止某些類型的工程。在設計裝修之前，請先審查附例。

常見問題

在溫哥華，我的分契物業裝修是否需要同時獲得strata審批和建築許可證？

是的。根據《卑詩省分契財產法》獲得strata corporation的批准和市政建築許可證是分開的要求。兩者都是必需的。Strata批准不能替代建築許可證，建築許可證也不能推翻strata附例。聚星裝修在溫哥華的每個分契物業裝修項目中都會處理這兩個流程。

如果我在未獲得strata批准的情況下裝修分契物業，會怎麼樣？

Strata corporation可以發出正式命令，要求您停止工程並自費將單位恢復到原始狀態。在嚴重情況下，strata可向卑詩省最高法院申請強制令。當您出售單位時，未批准的裝修可能需要披露，買方可以協商降價或要求將恢復原狀作為銷售的條件。

在卑詩省，strata批准需要多長時間？

Strata理事會有30天時間回覆裝修申請。如果裝修需要在大會上獲得3/4投票，請額外增加4-6週的通知和調度時間。從申請到獲得書面批准，整個過程通常需要6-10週，對於需要大會投票的裝修最多需要4個月。

溫哥華市對分契物業更換地板是否需要建築許可證？

是的，如果新地板材料比現有地板重得多。在溫哥華，用瓷磚、天然石材或混凝土面層更換乙烯基片材地板需要建築許可證，因為這會改變地板組裝的負荷。結構工程師評估會確認現有地板系統是否能支撐新材料。

計劃在大溫哥華的溫哥華、本拿比、列治文、素里、高貴林或其他城市裝修分契物業？聯絡聚星裝修獲取免費估價——strata審批、市政許可證和施工均包含在單一合同中。
